out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Cannot Exceed 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is being used as a control was not cooked, served or discarded by the expiration time as indicated: Sprout beans.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours is used as the public health control : 1) the food shall have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature or, 2) the food shall have an initial temperature of 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 3) the food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 4) the food shall be cooked and served, served if ready to eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 5) the food if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit shall be discarded. PIC was informed to keep and update log records on daily basis to maintain Time as a Public Health Control. PIC provided end points.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. EHS discussed that any staff preparing food shall wear hats or hair nets. PIC provided hair nets to the staff, and the staff complied by wearing them.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: Observed no date marking for cooked pork, garlic oil, cooked shrimp and etc. in WIC.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC understands all cooked/prepared foods kept for more than 24 hours must be date marked. PIC has date marked the aforementioned food items accordingly.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. Please provide a clearly visible poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands at the kitchen handwashing sink.

out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: observed cooked boba siting on the counter at service area at 84F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. EHS discussed with PIC that cooked boba (TCS) should be held at 135F and above, or held using Time as Public Health Control for not more than 4 hours. PIC agreed to use TPHC for the cooked boba and to maintain documentation for the initial temperature and the time the boba is discarded. EHS provided a copy of TPHC agreement to PIC.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Observed bean sprouts sitting on the counter at kitchen at 51F. EHS provided a copy of TPHC agreement to PIC.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS discussed with PIC that bean sprouts (TCS) should be held at 41F and below, or held using Time as Public Health Control for not more than 4 hours. PIC agreed to use TPHC for the bean sprouts and to maintain documentation for the initial temperature and the time the bean sprouts is discarded. EHS provided a copy of TPHC agreement to PIC. PIC placed sticky notes on bean sprouts container and will discard them in 3 hours.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: DOK Employee Health Policy
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide a verbal or written policy for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by an employee who has a disease or a medical condition. PIC did not have an employee health policy on site
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge or certified food manager is responsible for knowledge, of at least the primary foodborne diseases (the Big 6) and medical conditions, to determine possible restriction or exclusion of food employees. EHS provided a copy of an employee health policy

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: Cleaning Procedure
violations.observation: Observed food employees using improper handwashing procedures. EHS observed employee not properly washing hands between tasks
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wash their hands and exposed portions of their arms by: 1) discarding used gloves; 2) rinsing under warm running water; 3) applying soap; 4) rubbing together for at least 10-15 seconds; 5) rinsing thoroughly under warm running water; and 6) drying with paper towels or air drying device. EHS spoke to PIC about issue PIC corrected employee

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. EHS observed employee not changing gloves and following proper handwashing procedures between between changing tasks
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS spoke to PIC about issue PIC corrected employee, employee changed gloves and washed hands

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee was observed cleaning their hands in a food preparation sink, warewashing sink or in a mop sink. EHS observed multiple employees washing hands in the 3 compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. EHS spoke to PIC about issue, PIC corrected employees TEABREAK PHO & BOBA (Inspection Date: 11/06/2024) Page 3 of 6

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Poison/Toxic Material, Conditions of Use
violations.observation: Pesticides labeled for residential use were observed in the facility and are being applied by the operator to control pests. EHS observed household pesticide chemicals being stored in the kitchen area
violations.corrective_action: Remove residential use pesticides from the facility. When necessary for pest control, chemical pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. PIC disposed of household pesticide chemcials

violations.title: Storage-Personal Care Items
violations.observation: EHS observed medicine and other personal care items being stored above food prep areas
violations.corrective_action: All employees' personal care items shall be stored in a way that prevents the contamination of food and food contact surfaces through improper labeling or storage. PIC moved medicine from food prep areas and EHS discussed creating a separate location for storage of all personal items including vitamins, food, back packs, jackets, purses, etc.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: 1) Grilled onions are being stacked in a large stainless steel bowl and being placed on the floor.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS discussed cooling of hot foods using specific methods like shallow sheet pans and the walk-in refrigerator and/or walk-in freezer; not prep top units. Ensure correction before the follow up.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: EHS observed working containers of foods such as sugar, salt, dry spices, squeeze bottles, etc without labels on the containers
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS spoke to PIC about issue and will have all working containers, bulk bins, and bottles labeled before the follow up. TEABREAK PHO & BOBA (Inspection Date: 11/06/2024) Page 5 of 6

violations.title: Dead or Trapped Pest Removed
violations.observation: Dead or trapped roaches were found on the premises. EHS observed roaches being trapped on glue board
violations.corrective_action: Remove dead rodents, birds, and insects from the premises to ensure that the establishment is clean and sanitary and to prevent carcasses from attracting other pests. EHS spoke to PIC about issue

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: EHS observed food being stored on racks covered in tin foil that has not been changed in 24 hours
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. EHS spoke to PIC about issue

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. EHS observed onions, ginger, boxes of dry goods, oil being stored on the floor of the kitchen. EHS observed food being stored on the floors of the walk in cooler and freezer
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS spoke to PIC about issue. Ensure all food is 6 inches off the floor before the follow up. EHS discussed using dunnage racks.

violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall limit their jewelry to a plain wedding ring while preparing food. Food employees may not wear bracelets, watches, etc. because they can inhibit proper hand washing. EHS spoke to employees about the issue and will verify continued compliance at the follow up.

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints. EHS observed employee with no hair restraints
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. EHS spoke to employee about issue, employee put on hair restraint TEABREAK PHO & BOBA (Inspection Date: 11/06/2024) Page 4 of 6

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wipings Clothes Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter. EHS observed wet wiping cloths being stored on counter
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses PIC moved wiping cloths to sanitizer solution of bleach and water maintained at 50-200ppm. Ensure continued correction before the follow up.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: EHS observed dry good scoop, oil scoops and ice scoops being stored in a manner that they cannot be reached without contaminating food
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. Spoke to PIC about issue. PIC will ensure food scoops are stored with handles up at all times. Ensure correction before the follow up.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Observed pots (all sizes) stored on shelves in the kitchen not covered or inverted.
violations.corrective_action: Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored covered or inverted to prevent contamination. EHS discussed with PIC that all cleaned and sanitized equipment shall be stored inverted to allow for air drying and prevent contamination. Ensure correction before the follow up.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Handled Single-Service/Use Items Storage
violations.observation: Unwrapped knives, forks, or spoons were not stored in front kitchen with the handles up. Observed spoons being stored eating side up
violations.corrective_action: Knives, forks, and spoons that are not prewrapped shall be presented so that only the handles are touched by employees and consumers if consumer self- service is provided. Spoke to PIC about issue. EHS instructed PIC to turn the plastic spoons upside down.

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers for honey and jellies were observed reused for the storage of other foods.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. EHS discussed with the PIC to discontinue the reuse of these types of food containers as they are not designed for the ware washing process. Ensure correction before the follow up.

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items, Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed boxes of single service items stored directly on the floor in the hallway near the restrooms.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. EHS discussed getting more dunnage racks or shelving units for the hallway. Ensure correction before the follow up.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: 1) SURFACES BEING LINED WITH ALUMINUM FOIL.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. EHS DISCUSSED THE REMOVAL OF ALL ALUMINUM FOIL AS IT IS NOT WASHABLE. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: @REFRIGERATION@ EHS observed 2 door prep top not being able to maintain below 40F. Observed the unit at 55f.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. Spoke to PIC about issue. PIC will ensure repair to the unit and no food storage in the unit until maintaining an ambient air temperature of 34f-38f. Ensure correction before the follow up.

out_items.name: Hot and cold water available, adequate pressure

violations.title: Hot Water Capacity to Meet Peak Demands
violations.observation: Observed the 18kw water heater undersized for the hot water demands.
violations.corrective_action: Within 30 days, the permit holder shall replace or upgrade the water heater with a unit that meets the following design and capacity requirements: (1) Commercial grade, (2) Minimum of 50 gallon storage tank, (3) Minimum recovery rate of 136gph of 120f water at a 80F rise@, and (4) Specifications and installation meet National Sanitation Foundation (NSF) Standard 5. The permit holder shall provide the Health Department with the specifications (cut sheet) for the replacement water heater and obtain approval prior to purchase and installation. As an option, the permit holder may choose to remove a newly installed warewashing machine to comply with this requirement. Please be reminded that equipment replacement or addition is not allowed without prior approval by the Health Department. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT THE WATER HEATER IS UNDERSIZED. PLEASE PROVIDE A MINIMUM 30KW WATER HEATER WITHIN 30 DAYS.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Mops Allowed to Air Dry
violations.observation: Observed that mops are improperly stored between use. EHS observed mops being stored head down in buckets
violations.corrective_action: Store mops in a position that allows them to air dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. Spoke To PIC about issue,pic corrected mop storage
